country.comment: Study conducted in Amathole District Municipality (comprising six local municipalities: Amahlathi, Great Kei, Mbhashe, Mnquma, Ngqushwa, and Raymond Mhlaba) in the Eastern Cape Province, South Africa.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract (Setting); PDF p. 5, The study area & Figure 1

effect_estimate.comment: Primary empirical analysis is purely qualitative; descriptive percentages on household water and sanitation coverage (e.g., 30.14% no formal piped water, 17.24% piped inside dwelling, 13.39% inside yard, 30.25% communal piped <200 m, 8.89% communal piped >200 m; 21.66% no toilet) are cited from secondary municipal Integrated Development Plan (IDP) records.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. In Amathole District Municipality, water governance prioritised distributive infrastructure projects (boreholes, dams, standpipes, water carting) while neglecting procedural, quality, and outcome equity: tokenistic Integrated Development Plan (IDP) and budget consultations where few community inputs were adopted, weak ward councillor representation and accountability, and poor intergovernmental coordination across the two-tier division of powers between the district Water Service Authority and local municipalities (such as over access roads) led to project implementation delays, non-functioning completed water schemes and dry boreholes, inconsistent water tankering, and persistent rural–urban disparities in safe water and sanitation access (secondary 2019–2020 IDP figures cited show 30.14% of district households lacked formal piped water and 21.66% had no toilet).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract (Results & Conclusion); PDF pp. 6–11, Results and discussion & Conclusion

mechanism_certainty.comment: Qualitative case study (appraised with CASP Qualitative Checklist; design ceiling = 2) that directly observes and documents administrative and institutional governance mechanisms—including tokenistic IDP consultations, councillor representation gaps, and district–local municipal fragmentation over infrastructure responsibilities—operating on rural water project implementation and service access through interviews with 20 municipal officials, focus groups with 14 residents, and field observation.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 5–10, Research methods and design & Results and discussion

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines municipal Integrated Development Plan (IDP) and Water and Sanitation Development Plan (WSDP) processes (planning), urban–rural service delivery disparities and 200 m standpipe policy within the Water Service Authority jurisdiction (service_area), community and stakeholder consultation/representation via IDP roadshows and ward councillors (participation), two-tier division of powers and lack of coordination between the district municipality and local municipalities e.g. over access roads (institutional_fragmentation, political_coordination), resulting project implementation delays (delay), and failure to implement consequence management and audit accountability (sanction).
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, ENFORCEMENT, planning, service_area, delay, sanction, participation, institutional_fragmentation, political_coordination
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 5, The study area; PDF pp. 6–10, Results and discussion (especially Procedural fairness in water service provision, PDF pp. 9–10)

outcome_flags.comment: Empirically examines household access to safe drinking water and sanitation (water_access, sanitation_access), lack of formal piped water connections/sources (formal_connection), unequal urban–rural coverage across the six local municipalities (service_coverage), unreliable communal standpipes, boreholes, and inconsistent water tankering (service_reliability), water supply interruptions and intermittent supply with weeks/months between tank refills or dry taps (service_continuity), and prolonged delays in rural water project implementation (delay).
outcome_flags.value: water_access, sanitation_access, formal_connection, service_coverage, service_reliability, service_continuity, delay

study_design.comment: Constructivist exploratory qualitative case study combining primary interviews, focus groups, and field observation with secondary public records (IDP and audit reports), analysed inductively under four NAPA social equity themes.
study_design.value: Exploratory qualitative case study (semi-structured in-depth interviews, focus group discussions, participant observation, and secondary municipal document review with thematic analysis)
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract (Methods); PDF pp. 5–6, Research methods and design

evidence_quotes.quote: Setting: A rural district municipality in the Eastern Cape province, South Africa.
Methods: A constructivist exploratory qualitative case study research redesign was used.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 5, Research methods and design
evidence_quotes.quote: Two focus group discussions were held with community members (n = 14), and semi-structured in-depth interviews (n = 20) were conducted with municipal officials involved in water service provision (councillors, top management municipal officials, local municipality representatives, district municipality satellite representatives and Water Boards representatives).

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 7, Consistency in water service provision (quality equity)
evidence_quotes.quote: The tanks are not filled consistently, and they can go for weeks and months without being filled.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 9, Procedural fairness in water service provision
evidence_quotes.quote: We do Integrated Development Plan (IDP) and Budget roadshows, although very few inputs are considered because of the limited budget.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 10, Procedural fairness in water service provision
evidence_quotes.quote: Unfortunately, the same difficulties exist in the division of powers and functions between the district and local municipalities, resulting in project implementation delays, which may be traced back to coordination and consultation shortcomings.
